issue: Image decode has no decompression-bomb guard: `image::load_from_memory` will materialize a malicious multi-GB allocation from a small crafted PNG/GIF/TIFF before any size cap can fire.
evidence: let decoded = image::load_from_memory(bytes).ok()?;
suggested_fix: Construct an `ImageReader::from_memory(bytes)` and call `with_guessed_format(...).set_limits(image::Limits::default())` (or stricter, e.g. 64 MB decoded max) before loading. Currently the only defence is the upstream `file_read` size cap (100 MB raw bytes), which is the input size, not the decoded size.

issue: `default_user_data_dir_for` falls back to `/tmp/.aleph` when no home resolves; `/tmp` is world-writable, so a local attacker can pre-create `/tmp/.aleph/browser/chrome-mcp/<profile>/user-data-dir` as a symlink to redirect Chrome's profile dir (TOCTOU).
evidence: let root = crate::utils::paths::get_config_dir().unwrap_or_else(|_| std::path::PathBuf::from("/tmp/.aleph"));
suggested_fix: Refuse to launch when home resolution fails (return BrowserError), or use a directory under `/var/run/<uid>` / XDG_RUNTIME_DIR — never `/tmp` for security-sensitive state.

issue: `Drop` sends SIGKILL to recorded PIDs without verifying the PID still refers to the Chrome Aleph launched — PIDs are reused, so a later SIGKILL may kill an unrelated process owned by the same user.
evidence: for pid in pids { let rc = unsafe { libc::kill(pid as i32, libc::SIGKILL) }; }
suggested_fix: Track PIDs alongside their launch time and only signal when the start time matches; or use a process-group kill (kill(-pid)) so child processes share the fate; or store the `Child` handle and use `start_kill` on shutdown.

issue: Linux `is_chrome_running` uses `pgrep -x chrome`, missing Chromium (`chromium`/`chromium-browser`), Brave (`brave`/`brave-browser`) and Edge — false negative causes Aleph to launch its own Chrome alongside the user's existing browser.
evidence:
#[cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "macos")))]
std::process::Command::new("pgrep").arg("-x").arg("chrome")
suggested_fix: Iterate over CHROMIUM_NAMES from discovery.rs and probe each, or query a broader list (chrome|chromium|chromium-browser|brave-browser|msedge) with a single pgrep.

issue: Channel-binding cleanup error is logged with warn! and swallowed; on failure, channels keep pointing at the now-deleted agent (ghost-agent routing).
evidence: if let Err(e) = self.workspace_mgr.clear_bindings_for_agent(&args.agent_id) { warn!(agent_id = %args.agent_id, error = %e, "Failed to clear channel bindings for deleted agent"); }
suggested_fix: Surface the failure to the caller (return a degraded AgentDeleteOutput, or hard-error the delete) so the operator can re-run / manually clear, instead of a silent ghost-agent state.

issue: Wildcard match arm silently converts DB errors into 'default agent', masking store failures as unbound channels.
evidence: match self.workspace_mgr.get_active_agent(channel) { Ok(Some(id)) => Some(id), _ => Some(self.registry.default_agent_id().to_string()), }
suggested_fix: Distinguish Ok(None) (truly unbound → use default) from Err(...) (store failure → propagate as AlephError::Store so the caller sees the failure, not a phantom default).

issue: screen_record duration validation guards only `!is_finite()`; a negative but finite `duration` (e.g. -1.0) passes through and is then converted via `Duration::from_secs_f64` inside the limb, which panics on negative input — killing the worker.
evidence: `let duration_secs = match args.duration { Some(v) if !v.is_finite() => return Ok(Some(invalid_args(...))); Some(v) => v, None => 5.0 };` — followed by `let config = ... ScreenRecordConfig { duration_secs, ... }` and `screen.screen_record(config).await`. Same guard pattern in `desktop/shared/src/perception/screen_record.rs:537,830,936` and `desktop/macos/src/lib.rs:275,304` consumes it via `Duration::from_secs_f64`, which docs say panics on negative.
suggested_fix: Extend the guard to `!v.is_finite() || v < 0.0` (and ideally `v == 0.0`) before handing `duration_secs` to the limb, or saturate at `0.0` in the tool layer as `desktop/windows/src/media.rs:78-82` and `desktop/linux/src/media.rs:553` already do on the platform side.

issue: `execute_batch_move` calls blocking `fs::rename` (and `fs::metadata`) inside an async function while a `lock_path_pair` guard is held — every rename on a slow/network filesystem stalls a tokio worker and blocks any concurrent task waiting on the same path lock.
evidence: let _path_guards = crate::tools::path_locks::lock_path_pair(&src_canonical, &dest_path).await; ... match fs::rename(&path, &dest_path) {
suggested_fix: Switch to `tokio::fs::rename` and `tokio::fs::metadata`, or wrap the rename in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`. The path lock should be released before any blocking syscall that does not need cross-task coordination across an `.await`.

issue: `execute_organize` calls blocking `fs::read_dir`, `fs::create_dir`, `fs::rename`, `fs::metadata` inside an async function, blocking tokio workers — same failure mode `stats::count_lines` was specifically rewritten to avoid.
evidence: let entries: Vec<_> = fs::read_dir(&canonical) ... fs::rename(&path, &dest_path)
suggested_fix: Move the walk + rename loop into `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`, or convert to `tokio::fs` calls. The `count_lines` precedent (audit BTS-5) shows this exact issue already caused 'wedged executor' in production.

issue: `execute_list` calls blocking `fs::read_dir` and `entry.metadata()` inside an async function. On a directory with many entries (e.g. `node_modules/`, a build cache), the entire walk happens on a tokio worker thread.
evidence: for entry in fs::read_dir(&canonical) ... let Ok(metadata) = entry.metadata() else {
suggested_fix: Use `tokio::fs::read_dir` and `entry.metadata().await`, or move the walk into `spawn_blocking` as `stats::count_lines` does.

issue: `read_file_bytes` calls blocking `fs::metadata` and `fs::read` inside an async function — a multi-second read on a slow/network filesystem stalls a tokio worker.
evidence: let metadata = fs::metadata(&canonical) ... let bytes = fs::read(&canonical)
suggested_fix: Use `tokio::fs::metadata` and `tokio::fs::read`.

issue: `execute_move` calls blocking `fs::rename` inside an async function (and while holding the path lock).
evidence: fs::rename(&from_canonical, &to_canonical)
suggested_fix: Switch to `tokio::fs::rename`.

issue: `execute_copy` calls blocking `fs::copy`, `fs::create_dir_all`, `fs::canonicalize`, `fs::read_dir`, `fs::copy` inside async functions (the recursive helper runs on the same executor).
evidence: tally.bytes = fs::copy(&from_canonical, &to_canonical) ... copy_dir_recursive(...)
suggested_fix: Either migrate the recursive walker to `tokio::fs` calls (lots of churn), or move the whole copy into a single `spawn_blocking` — the entire operation is I/O-bound and benefits from blocking-pool scheduling more than from cooperative scheduling.

issue: `execute_delete` calls blocking `fs::remove_file`, `fs::remove_dir_all`, and `count_path_entries` (which itself calls `fs::read_dir` recursively) inside an async function while holding the path lock.
evidence: fs::remove_file(&canonical) ... fs::remove_dir_all(&canonical)
suggested_fix: Either migrate to `tokio::fs` (the recursive tree-walk is awkward to port) or wrap the whole deletion in a single `spawn_blocking`. Note that holding the per-path lock across a multi-second blocking call defeats the lock's purpose of protecting concurrent edits.

issue: `execute_mkdir` calls blocking `fs::create_dir_all`/`fs::create_dir` and uses `canonical.exists()` / `canonical.is_dir()` (blocking stat) inside an async function while holding the path lock.
evidence: if canonical.exists() { ... fs::create_dir_all(&canonical)
suggested_fix: Use `tokio::fs` equivalents; the exists/is_dir checks should also be async stat calls.

issue: Store lookup error silently defaults the new note_path to `format!("other/{safe_new}")`, which is wrong on store failure AND on a successful rename into a non-'other' category — destination receipt then points to a nonexistent path.
evidence: .find_by_filename(&safe_new, agent_id).await.unwrap_or_default();  let note_path = new_paths.first().cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| format!("other/{safe_new}"));
suggested_fix: Propagate the store error via AlephError::tool; on Ok(empty) distinguish 'rename did not register yet' (retry) from 'wrong category guess' (refuse to fabricate a path).

issue: Per-note body read errors are silently dropped to empty string; the note still counts as a hit (fts_candidates) but renders as an empty body, corrupting the 'what did query find' signal the model relies on.
evidence: async move { tokio::fs::read_to_string(&path).await.unwrap_or_default() }
suggested_fix: Surface the read failure (or attach a 'body unreadable' marker per-row) and decrement fts_candidates or emit a bodies_omitted count so the advisory reflects reality.

issue: pub fn generate(...) is sync CPU+IO (markdown parse, font file read, PDF build, std::fs::write) called directly from async fn call() in mod.rs — blocks the tokio executor thread on every PDF.
evidence: RenderEngine::Native => native_engine::generate(&args, &output_path), // called from async fn call
suggested_fix: Wrap the body in tokio::task::spawn_blocking and await the JoinHandle; keep the public signature async so the executor is not starved during long renders.

issue: PDF write is non-atomic, non-fsynced std::fs::write — a crash mid-write leaves a truncated/zero-byte file at output_path with no way for the caller to tell 'partial write' from 'no data'.
evidence: std::fs::write(output_path, &pdf_bytes).map_err(|e| ToolError::Execution(format!("Failed to write PDF file: {e}")))?;
suggested_fix: Write to a sibling tempfile, fsync, then atomic-rename onto output_path; call File::sync_all() before close so the bytes hit disk before the rename.

issue: No authorization check — any caller can approve or reject any worker's shutdown request.
evidence: let leader_id = if actor.is_empty() { "leader".to_string() } else { actor }; — same pattern as plan_resolve, no team-leader resolution.
suggested_fix: Resolve the team's leader via TeamStore and require caller == leader; otherwise refuse.

issue: No authorization check — any caller can approve or reject any team's submitted plans via plan_manager.approve_plan / reject_plan.
evidence: let leader_id = if actor.is_empty() { "leader" } else { &actor }; — no team-leader resolution or comparison; literal "leader" used when actor is empty.
suggested_fix: Resolve team.leader_id via TeamStore and compare against self.actor(); refuse non-leaders with a same-shape not-found error.

issue: No authorization check — any caller can start a multi-turn collaborative session on any team with arbitrary participants.
evidence: let session = self.coordinator.start_session(input, &self.actor()).await — no leader/team-membership gate; participants are caller-controlled.
suggested_fix: Require caller to be the team's leader (or a member) before starting; validate participant list against team membership.

issue: No authorization check — any caller can read any team's full collaborative session transcript (multi-turn agent-to-agent content).
evidence: let session = self.store.get_session(&args.session_id).await?... — no team membership check; transcript is rendered verbatim into the tool output.
suggested_fix: Resolve session.team_id, then check team membership / participation before returning the transcript.

issue: No authorization check — any caller can submit a turn, conclude, or cancel any team's collaborative session.
evidence: match args.mode.as_str() { "respond" => self.coordinator.submit_turn(...).await, "conclude" => self.coordinator.finalize(...), "cancel" => self.coordinator.cancel(...) } — no participant/leader gate.
suggested_fix: For respond/conclude require the caller to be a session participant; for cancel require leader or participant.

issue: No authorization check — any caller can set or clear any team's operating protocol, which is injected verbatim into every member's launch context.
evidence: self.store.set_protocol(&args.team_id, args.protocol.clone()).await? — no leader/team-membership check before the write.
suggested_fix: Resolve team and require leader == actor; refuse foreign team ids with not-found shape.

issue: No authorization check on any snapshot operation — any caller can list, get, restore, or delete any team's snapshots.
evidence: fn call(&self, args: Self::Args) -> Result<Self::Output> { ... match args.action { SnapshotAction::Create => { ... } ... } } — no leader/team-membership gate before capture_snapshot / restore_snapshot / delete
suggested_fix: Add a leader-only / team-membership gate mirroring `task_team_reachable` before each action arm; refuses must read like a missing snapshot for foreign teams.

issue: DNS rebinding TOCTOU window in the fetch provider path: validate_url_async pins a SocketAddr, but the pin is discarded and the operator-hosted provider performs its own DNS resolution inside the protected network.
evidence: match validate_url_async(&args.url, &self.ssrf_policy).await { Ok((_url, _pinned)) => { warn!(..."fetch provider path does not thread the validated DNS pin; provider performs its own resolution (SSRF host-policy gate enforced, IP-pin TOCTOU window remains)") } ... for provider in &self.fetch_providers { match provider.fetch(&args.url).await { ... } }
suggested_fix: Extend the FetchProvider trait to accept a pre-resolved SocketAddr (or pin via a Host header override / custom resolver) so the provider cannot connect to a different IP than the one the SSRF gate validated.

issue: Skill extraction follows symlinks at the destination directory, allowing an attacker-planted symlink under skills_dir/<name> to redirect bundled files anywhere on disk.
evidence: fn extract_dir_recursive(dir: &Dir, target: &Path) -> std::io::Result<()> { std::fs::create_dir_all(target)?; extract_dir_contents(dir, target)?; ... } — no symlink_metadata(target) guard. compare_plugin hardening at prepare_plugin_temp_dir (line 394) which explicitly rejects symlinks with the comment "a user-planted symlink at the temp path must be removed BEFORE create_dir_all, otherwise the staging copy writes through the symlink and lands outside the cache"; the same defense is missing here and in copy_tree_with_prune (line 661).
suggested_fix: At the top of extract_dir_recursive (and copy_tree_with_prune) do `if let Ok(m) = std::fs::symlink_metadata(target) { if m.file_type().is_symlink() { return Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput, ...)) } }` — mirror prepare_plugin_temp_dir's pattern.

issue: `emulate` serializes `extra_http_headers` to a JSON string (`serde_json::to_string(headers)`) and passes it as `extraHttpHeaders` — wire contract with the MCP server is unverified by a test, mirroring the `wait_for` text-vs-list shape defect that broke the same backend.
evidence: let encoded = serde_json::to_string(headers)... args.insert("extraHttpHeaders".into(), json!(encoded));
suggested_fix: Pin the wire shape with an integration test against a fake server (same approach as the wait_for/fill_form pinning tests) or check the MCP server's published schema explicitly.

issue: `screenshot` fallback path detects error text by string-prefix on `error`/`failed:`/`permission denied`/`access denied`; the underlying MCP server contract isn't pinned by a test, so a server wording change silently regresses to base64-decode errors.
evidence: if head_lower.starts_with("error") || head_lower.starts_with("failed:") || head_lower.starts_with("permission denied") || head_lower.starts_with("access denied")
suggested_fix: Probe the JSON content type array shape first (image vs text) and only attempt base64 on confirmed image responses; treat empty text + no image as failure without heuristics.

issue: `wait_for` releases the per-profile serialization lock before issuing the MCP `wait_for` call so concurrent ops don't stall; a concurrent `select_page` on the same profile during the up-to-120s wait re-targets the wait at a different page (documented trade-off, but worth a re-target lock or wait-bound tab id).
evidence: { let _guard = self.profile_guard().await; self.select_page(tab_id).await?; } let outcome = self.call("wait_for", wait_for_args(text, timeout_ms)).await;
suggested_fix: Either accept the documented race or pass the tab id into the MCP `wait_for` call (if supported server-side) so the wait binds to the tab not the page-selection.

issue: `screenshot` writes its temp file to `std::env::temp_dir()` (`/tmp/aleph-ss-<uuid>.{png,jpg}`) — outside Aleph's `~/.aleph/data/browser` containment and the file_ops gate. A successful screenshot reads then `remove_file`s it, but if the process dies between `read` and `remove`, the temp file lingers indefinitely in `/tmp`.
evidence: let mut path = std::env::temp_dir(); let fname = format!("aleph-ss-{}.{ext}", uuid::Uuid::new_v4()); path.push(fname);
suggested_fix: Write under `browser_state_dir("cli-screenshots")` (consistent with `playwright_launch::output_dir_for` and `config_path_for`), or add a startup `sweep_tmp_aleph_ss_files` task.

issue: unwrap_or_default on IDENTITY.md read silently treats PermissionDenied / corrupt-UTF8 reads as 'empty file', then overwrites the original with a partial reconstruction.
evidence: let existing = std::fs::read_to_string(identity_path).unwrap_or_default();
suggested_fix: Distinguish NotFound (truly empty) from other IO errors (propagate). Use map_err and let permission errors surface instead of silently appending to a file the caller cannot read.

issue: bindings_by_agent() Result is silently defaulted on Err, hiding store failures from the LLM that uses 'bound_channels' for routing decisions.
evidence: let bindings = self.workspace_mgr.bindings_by_agent().unwrap_or_default();
suggested_fix: At minimum log the error (warn!); better: propagate via AlephError::Store so the channel binding surface is observably broken rather than reporting 'no bindings'.

issue: MAX_EXEC_BUDGET_MS = 600_000 is implicitly coupled to harness BUILTIN_TOOL_BUDGETS_MS being > 600_000ms; the coupling is documented in a comment but not enforced
evidence: const MAX_EXEC_BUDGET_MS: u64 = 600_000; with a comment that the harness table now carries 'browser_exec' with headroom above this number. If a future change to BUILTIN_TOOL_BUDGETS_MS drops the value below 600s, this budget becomes unreachable in practice (killed by the harness first).
suggested_fix: Add a test or compile-time assertion that pulls BUILTIN_TOOL_BUDGETS_MS[name = browser_exec] and asserts it > MAX_EXEC_BUDGET_MS. Or invert the relationship: define BUILTIN_TOOL_BUDGETS_MS for browser_exec as `MAX_EXEC_BUDGET_MS + headroom` so the relationship is expressed once.

issue: bound_content_head_tail calls text.chars().count() up to 3 times in a hot path (console/network reads)
evidence: let total_chars = text.chars().count(); ... elided = total_chars.saturating_sub(head.chars().count()).saturating_sub(tail.chars().count()); — each .chars().count() is O(n); on a 30k-char input the function does 3 full unicode-aware scans when one suffices.
suggested_fix: Walk char_indices() once into a Vec, or compute head.chars().count() from the budget (head_budget) and tail.chars().count() from tail_budget. The elided count is total_chars - head_chars - tail_chars; head_chars is bounded by head_budget and tail_chars by tail_budget, so the multi-pass scan is unnecessary.

issue: `run_boundary_crossed` clears held desktop inputs only for the *current* session (`held_inputs::release_all(&held_inputs::current_session_id(), screen)`). A previous run that died with a stuck key on a *different* session_id keeps its input held forever — only an Escape press drains the whole ledger. The cross-session `release_all_sessions` exists but is wired only to the Escape path.
evidence: In `mod.rs::DesktopTool::check_escape`: run-boundary arm calls `held_inputs::release_all(&held_inputs::current_session_id(), screen).await`; Escape arm calls `held_inputs::release_all_sessions(screen).await`. Session id is `turn_context::current_turn_context().session_key.to_key_string()` — a new run is not guaranteed to share it with the dead one.
suggested_fix: Either call `release_all_sessions` on the run-boundary arm too, or, less invasive, expire ledger entries older than a TTL on boundary.

issue: `check_blocked_app` falls back to the frontmost-app check on `resolve_rail` Err. When the actual failure is "app not found / ambiguous", and the *frontmost* app happens to be a password manager, the model is told "computer use is blocked in credential vaults — ask the user" instead of the real rail-resolution message. Dispatch will refuse with the better message, but the guard runs first and shadows it.
evidence: `let target = match rail { Ok(native::Rail::Targeted(pid)) => { ... apps.iter().find(|a| a.pid == Some(pid))? } Ok(native::Rail::Global) | Err(_) => apps.iter().find(|a| a.is_active)? }; safety::blocked_app_reason(&target.name, &target.bundle_id).map(...)` — the `Err(_) =>` arm intentionally conservatively assumes the global tap. Comment in code acknowledges the choice but does not address the shadowing.
suggested_fix: On `Err(_)` from `resolve_rail`, return early `None` so the dispatch refusal surfaces; only fall back to frontmost on `Ok(Rail::Global)`.

issue: The `observe:"screenshot"` path calls `call_via_platform` recursively for a post-action screenshot, but only checks `if let Ok(Some(shot))` — the inner screenshot's `data` is silently dropped on any failure (budget, error, no platform). The outer mutating action still reports `success:true`, with `post_screenshot` simply absent and no `message` warning. A model that asked for an `observe` screenshot gets no signal that the observation never happened.
evidence: `if args.observe.as_deref() == Some("screenshot") { ... let mut shot_args = ...; if let Ok(Some(shot)) = self.call_via_platform(platform, &shot_args).await { if let (Some(obj), Some(shot_data)) = (... output.data.as_mut()..., shot.data) { obj.insert("post_screenshot".into(), shot_data); } } }` — no `else` arm, no log, no message.
suggested_fix: Add an `else` arm that inserts a `post_screenshot_failed` field with the inner error message (or at minimum logs `tracing::warn!`), so a missing screenshot is not silently indistinguishable from one that took.

issue: `execute_batch_move` uses `file_name().unwrap_or_default()` and passes the empty `OsStr` through `replace(['/', '\\'], "_")` (no-op), then `unique_dest(dest_canonical, "")` returns `dest_canonical` itself. The subsequent `fs::rename(file, dest_dir)` is harmless (the rename fails), but a model-targeted glob pattern that matches e.g. a pathless entry silently turns into a no-op with no error surfaced.
evidence: let file_name = path.file_name().unwrap_or_default(); let safe_name = file_name.to_string_lossy().replace(['/', '\\'], "_");
suggested_fix: If `file_name()` returns empty, treat the entry as malformed and continue (or push to `errors`). Don't pass "" into `unique_dest`.

issue: `execute_search` calls blocking `fs::metadata(&path)` inside an async function for every glob match — `glob::glob` is sync, but the per-match stat should not block the worker.
evidence: if let Ok(metadata) = fs::metadata(&path) {
suggested_fix: Use `tokio::fs::metadata` (or `spawn_blocking` over the whole `for entry in glob::glob` loop).

issue: Provenance/audit-trail write has no error handling — a silent failure here means the install is on disk but the audit ledger says it never happened.
evidence: crate::hub::origin::record_install(&self.cache, entry, spec, &outcome).await;
suggested_fix: Wrap in if let Err(e) = ... { tracing::warn!(...); } at minimum, or surface as a verification report field so the model can flag a missing audit.

issue: serde_json serialization failure is silently converted to Value::Null, hiding malformed-output bugs and producing an empty `data` field on the wire.
evidence: let data = serde_json::to_value(&output).unwrap_or_default();
suggested_fix: Surface as ToolError::Execution so the LLM sees the bug rather than getting a null payload that looks like 'no extractable content'.

issue: Same silent-swallow serialization pattern as document_extract: Value::Null on failure masks provider-output bugs.
evidence: let data = serde_json::to_value(&output).unwrap_or_default();
suggested_fix: Same as document_extract: return ToolError::Execution on serialization failure.

issue: Invalid `scope` values (anything not 'all'/'current_session'/'both') silently return empty results — no error, no warning — because both string-comparison branches evaluate false.
evidence: let scope = args.scope.as_deref().unwrap_or("all"); ... if scope == "current_session" || scope == "both" { ... } else if scope == "all" || scope == "both" { ... }
suggested_fix: Define an enum `MemorySearchScope { All, CurrentSession, Both }` with `Deserialize` and validate the wire form up front, returning `AlephError::tool` for any other value. The closed-vocabulary string-match across three sites will otherwise drift if a new scope is added.

issue: agent_id traversal guard rejects '..', '/', '\\', leading '.', but NOT null bytes — on Linux EINVAL from Path join; on Windows the path is silently truncated, which could land a note in an unintended vault directory.
evidence: if id.is_empty() || id.contains("..") || id.contains('/') || id.contains('\\') || id.starts_with('.') { ... }
suggested_fix: Add `|| id.contains('\0')` to the rejection set; consider also adding Windows-reserved-name / colon checks for cross-platform safety.

issue: The secret-prefix list is hand-maintained and duplicated from the finished-path scrubber — adding a new provider to one list without the other creates a live leak that the other surface catches.
evidence: const PREFIXES: &[&[u8]] = &[b"sk-ant-", b"sk-proj-", b"sk-", b"AKIA", b"ASIA", b"ghp_", b"gho_", b"ghs_", b"glpat-", b"xoxb-", b"xoxp-"];
suggested_fix: Extract a single shared `known_secret_prefixes()` accessor in the scrub module and call it from both call sites; the comment in the function already names this duplication risk.

issue: Disband relies only on requires_confirmation (UX safeguard) — no team-leadership check, so any agent can trigger a disband that cancels sessions and expires messages for any team once a human clicks Confirm.
evidence: fn requires_confirmation(&self) -> bool { true } followed by self.store.disband_team(&args.team_id).await? with no team-leader resolution.
suggested_fix: Resolve team.leader_id and refuse non-leaders before any state mutation; requires_confirmation stays as a second safeguard.

issue: No authorization check — any caller can read any team's full state (members, task ids/subjects, statuses, results, protocol).
evidence: let team = self.store.get_team(&args.team_id).await?... — no membership check; output includes task subjects and result strings verbatim.
suggested_fix: Apply the same ownership pattern used by `task_team_reachable` — refuse foreign team ids with the same not-found shape.

issue: No ownership gate when listing artifacts by task_id — an agent that knows another team's task_id can list all artifacts under it (task_id is LLM-supplied).
evidence: let artifacts = self.store.get_artifacts_for_task(&args.task_id).await?... — direct list path has no team-membership check; the single-artifact path only verifies artifact.task_id == args.task_id.
suggested_fix: Resolve task.team_id via the coord store (when wired) and apply task_team_reachable before returning artifacts.

issue: No authorization check — any caller can read any team's event log (subjects, decisions, attachments, agent ids).
evidence: let events = self.event_store.get_events(&args.team_id, Some(since), Some(now)).await? — no membership check before fetching and rendering events.
suggested_fix: Resolve team and require the caller be a member before reading events.

issue: Validates team existence but no membership/authz check — any caller can read any team's token usage breakdown.
evidence: let _team = self.team_store.get_team(&args.team_id).await?... — only existence is checked; the agent_ids list and per-agent usage rollups are returned regardless of caller identity.
suggested_fix: Require caller membership in the team before returning per-agent breakdown; refuse foreign teams with not-found shape.

issue: No authorization check — any caller can toggle voice mode (and reset failure counters) on any channel via LLM-supplied channel_id.
evidence: self.channel_registry.update_voice_state(&channel_id, |state| { state.enabled = enabled; ... state.consecutive_failures = 0; }).await — no actor-vs-channel ownership check.
suggested_fix: Constrain channel_id to one the calling agent owns / is permitted to manage, or require channel-scoped permission.

issue: Mutex poison recovery `unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())` silently serves the cache after a previous holder panicked — possibly inconsistent state.
evidence: let mut guard = URL_CACHE.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()); — both cache_lookup and cache_store recover from poisoning without logging or clearing.
suggested_fix: Log the poisoning event and clear the cache on recovery (or restart the cache) so post-panic inconsistencies cannot be served.

issue: reconcile() counts per-entry read_dir / symlink_metadata errors in a Cell and logs them, but still proceeds to retain() — quietly dropping the affected entries from the manifest on the next save, losing provenance.
evidence: // Per-entry errors during the read_dir iteration are counted and logged: silently dropping them would let a race-on-unlink or a permissions glitch on a subdir classify the affected entry as "removed" and remove it from the manifest on the next save ... pub fn reconcile(&mut self, skills_dir: &Path) -> std::io::Result<()> { ... self.skills.retain(|name, _| on_disk.contains(name)); ... }
suggested_fix: Either return Err from reconcile when skip_count > 0 (caller skips save), or carry a `dirty` flag forward so callers don't call save() after a partial reconcile. The current 'log but proceed' shape silently reaps provenance on a transient permissions error.

issue: clone_or_update has a TOCTOU race on the .git existence check; two concurrent invocations for the same checkout_dir both observe existed=false and both call Repository::clone.
evidence: let existed = checkout_dir.join(".git").exists(); ... let repo = if existed { git2::Repository::open(checkout_dir) ... } else { ... git2::Repository::clone(repo_url, checkout_dir) ... }; — explicit only check is unsynchronized; the doc says "call from spawn_blocking" but does not say single-flight.
suggested_fix: Serialize the (repo_url, checkout_dir) pair via a manager-level DashMap/mutex keyed by checkout_dir, or wrap the exist-check-and-clone in a file lock (flock on the checkout_dir itself). At minimum, surface the second-clone error rather than panicking with a confusing libgit2 message.

issue: TOCTOU between `tokio::fs::metadata(&path)` and the subsequent `atomic_write_bytes`. The per-canvas lock blocks in-process races, but an external process (operator, sync client) can swap a file for a directory between the check and the write, turning the dedupe branch into a failed write that leaves the caller's bytes unstored.
evidence: let dedupe_hit = match tokio::fs::metadata(&path).await { ... atomic_write_bytes(&path, bytes)
suggested_fix: Open with `O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW` semantics (via `tokio::fs::OpenOptions::new().create_new(true).write(true)`), treat `AlreadyExists` as a dedupe hit, and fall back to overwriting only after confirming the inode is still a regular file.

issue: Orphan sweep runs INSIDE the per-canvas critical section, so a slow `read_dir` over a large `assets/` dir blocks every other `apply` on the same canvas.
evidence: if let Err(e) = self.sweep_assets_with(id, &referenced).await {
suggested_fix: Move the sweep call to AFTER `drop(guard)`. The `referenced` set is already an owned `HashSet<String>` and the asset filesystem is independent of the doc, so holding the lock while sweeping only serializes for no correctness gain.

issue: `delete` calls `tokio::fs::remove_dir_all` while still holding the per-canvas write lock; for a canvas with many assets this is unbounded wall-time inside the critical section.
evidence: tokio::fs::remove_dir_all(self.root.join(id))
suggested_fix: Stage the delete under a separate `delete-pending` marker inside the lock, drop the guard, then perform `remove_dir_all` and verify the marker survived (or repeat if a concurrent create stole the id).

issue: Event publish clones the full op batch on every apply (`ops.to_vec()`), bounded by `MAX_OPS_PER_APPLY` but unnecessary because the caller already owns the slice until `apply` returns.
evidence: ops: ops.to_vec(),
suggested_fix: Have `emit_updated` take `Vec<CanvasOp>` and pass `ops.to_vec()` once at the top of `apply` if the bus cannot borrow, or pass an `Arc<Vec<CanvasOp>>` to avoid cloning per-subscriber.

issue: `apply_ops` mutates `doc.shapes`, `doc.title`, `doc.decks` in place BEFORE the post-state `MAX_SHAPES` check. The partial mutation is safe because the caller drops the guard uncommitted, but the function name gives no signal that failure leaves the doc half-rewritten in memory.
evidence: doc.shapes.push(shape.clone()) ... if doc.shapes.len() > MAX_SHAPES { return Err(...) }
suggested_fix: Either rename to `try_apply_ops` and document the side-effect contract, or pre-validate the count (e.g. simulate the cap delta over the op list) before mutating.

issue: `looks_like_transport_error` calls `s.contains(n)` then `s.find(n)` — two linear scans per needle instead of one; trivially replaceable with a single find-iteration.
evidence: if s.contains(n) { if let Some(idx) = s.find(n) { ... } }
suggested_fix: Drop the `contains` call and pattern-match on `find` directly.

issue: `ensure_chrome_running` failure path loses context — the error from the initial MCP connect (`tracing::info!` discards it) is followed by a fresh `AttachFailed`, so an operator cannot see what made the first connect fail (only that the retry path failed too).
evidence: tracing::info!("Chrome DevTools MCP connection failed, attempting to launch Chrome: {e}"); ... BrowserError::AttachFailed(format!("Failed to connect Chrome DevTools MCP after launching Chrome: {e}"))
suggested_fix: Chain the original error into the AttachFailed message (e.g. `format!("... after launching Chrome (initial connect: {initial_e}): {retry_e}")`).

issue: `select_page` parses `tab_id` as `u32`; tab ids larger than u32::MAX (or with leading zeros) silently fail with a `TabNotFound`-shaped error that doesn't explain the actual reason (parse error vs. genuine absence).
evidence: let page_id: u32 = tab_id.parse().map_err(|_| BrowserError::ActionFailed(format!("Invalid tab ID '{tab_id}': expected numeric page ID")))?;
suggested_fix: Use `str::parse::<u32>()` then map the parse error to a dedicated `InvalidTabId` variant or include the parse error in the message.

issue: `spawn_idle_reaper`'s claim-or-skip check uses `existing.strong_count() > 0`, which is a non-atomic read against the same Arc the next line downgrades — under contention the count can go to zero between the check and the downgrade, causing a brief window where the slot is stolen from a manager that just dropped its last owner.
evidence: match slot.as_ref() { Some(existing) if existing.strong_count() > 0 => { ... return; } Some(_) | None => { ... } }
suggested_fix: Use `Arc::ptr_eq` against a stored sentinel or accept the race (acceptable since stealing a dying manager's slot is harmless — only flags it as a finding).

issue: Duplicated `const fn default_true() -> bool { true }` between `network_policy.rs` and `profile.rs` — same one-line constant declared twice.
evidence: src/browser/network_policy.rs:112  const fn default_true() -> bool { true }  / src/browser/profile.rs:139  const fn default_true() -> bool { true }
suggested_fix: Hoist into `src/utils/` (or `types.rs`) and import from both sites.

issue: `spawn` reads the child's stdout/stderr via `child.wait_with_output()` under a tokio timeout — if the child fills its pipe buffers before being read, the process blocks on write and the timeout never trips because the read side never yields.
evidence: let output_fut = child.wait_with_output(); let output = match tokio::time::timeout(timeout, output_fut).await { ... }
suggested_fix: Spawn a background drain task that continuously reads stdout/stderr into bounded `Vec<u8>`s while `wait()` runs, so pipe pressure cannot deadlock the child.

issue: Inner `default_screenshot_format` free function is `pub(super)`-equivalent — only used by `impl Default for ScreenshotOpts`. Inline it into the Default impl or behind a single const.
evidence: fn default_screenshot_format() -> String { "png".to_string() } impl Default for ScreenshotOpts { fn default() -> Self { Self { ..., format: default_screenshot_format(), } } }
suggested_fix: Inline as `format: String::from("png")` (or const `SCREENSHOT_DEFAULT_FORMAT: &str = "png"`); serde's `default = "..."` must point to a function but the Default impl can construct directly.

issue: The SSRF pre-flight uses `SsrfPolicy::default()` rather than the live `Config`-derived policy, so operator allow/deny rules on the SSRF panel do not propagate to `a2a_agents(add=…)`.
evidence: validate_url_async(&url, &SsrfPolicy::default())
suggested_fix: Pass the policy built from `crate::config::Config::ssrf` (the same `Config` `web_fetch` consults) so the operator's audit `config_audit` findings and the actual enforcement share a single source. A `default()` here means the audit tool can report "allow_private_network=true is dangerous" while `a2a_agents.add` still blocks private IPs — and vice versa.

issue: `bash_exec.rs:316` spawns a detached task that re-enters three task-locals (`SESSION_ID`, `LIVE_TAIL`, exec workspace) and a `CallIdentity`; the scope ordering is correct today but the `tokio::spawn` boundary means any future field added to the harness MUST also be re-entered or silently leak.
evidence: let join = tokio::spawn(async move { ... LIVE_TAIL.scope(live_for_task, async move { crate::sandbox::context::with_exec_workspace(...) ... SESSION_ID.scope(sid, ...) }) });
suggested_fix: Add a compile-time test that asserts every task-local set on the foreground side of `spawn_background` is also re-entered inside the task (`include_str!` over the file and a list of `.scope(` calls). The current behavioural test catches a leak of `LIVE_TAIL`; it does not catch a leak of `CallIdentity` or a future task-local.

issue: resolve_target uses if let Some(ref rid) = args.ref_id followed by rid.clone() — slightly clunky
evidence: if let Some(ref rid) = args.ref_id { Ok(ActionTarget::Ref { ref_id: rid.clone() }) } else if let (Some(x), Some(y)) = (args.x, args.y) { ... }
suggested_fix: args.ref_id.clone().map(|rid| ActionTarget::Ref { ref_id: rid }).ok_or(...) chained with the coordinate branch. Pure idiom nit, not a bug.

issue: backend_error_text is named to take &BrowserError but the body re-formats via err.to_string() before bounding, then sanitize_external_text on the bounded output
evidence: let raw = err.to_string(); let (bounded, truncated) = bound_content_head_tail(&raw, MAX_BACKEND_ERROR_CHARS); let scrubbed = sanitize_external_text(&manager.redact_content(&bounded)); — the to_string() could in theory pre-truncate the error, but the bound_content_head_tail then runs again, so the head/tail split is on the full string. Functionally correct, just two passes.
suggested_fix: Inline the bound_content_head_tail call against the raw, then redact+scrub. The current double-pass is fine on 2k chars but could be a one-pass for clarity.

issue: bound_content always allocates a new String even when input is within budget
evidence: return (text.to_string(), false) and (text[..cut].to_string(), true) — the within-budget branch is hit on the vast majority of reads and forces an unconditional allocation/copy.
suggested_fix: Return Cow<'_, str>: Cow::Borrowed(text) when within budget, Cow::Owned when truncated. Callers either re-string-format (cheap on Borrowed) or can branch on truncation separately.

issue: process_evaluate_result always returns Value::String, making the Value::String(s) => s match-arm in exec.rs::run_one Evaluate branch's `other => other.to_string()` fallback dead code
evidence: mod.rs process_evaluate_result always wraps in serde_json::Value::String(redact_and_wrap(...)); exec.rs::run_one PlannedAction::Evaluate then matches serde_json::Value::String(s) => s (live) and `other => other.to_string()` (unreachable).
suggested_fix: Change process_evaluate_result to return String directly, or document that exec.rs's `other` arm is a defensive future-proofing. Either way, the unreachable arm in exec.rs can be a clippy::diverging_sub_expression or similar nit.

issue: bound_screenshot_png iterative downscale scales [0.7, 0.5, 0.35, 0.25] are inline literals; the 0.25 floor is documented but produces a soft (not hard) byte cap
evidence: for scale in [0.7_f64, 0.5, 0.35, 0.25] { ... if attempt.len() <= MAX_SCREENSHOT_BYTES { return attempt; } ... } smallest — the final return is `smallest` which may exceed MAX_SCREENSHOT_BYTES.
suggested_fix: Either (a) name the scale sequence as a `const SCALE_STEPS: &[f64] = &[0.7, 0.5, 0.35, 0.25];` near the byte cap constant, or (b) drop the 'over-budget is better than nothing' comment out of the code into a doc-comment on a named `MIN_SCREENSHOT_DIMENSION` constant. The trade-off itself is fine; the inline magic numbers are the issue.

issue: wrap_describe_layers discards the truncation bool from bound_content, so the model is not told the description was truncated
evidence: description.map(|t| { let (bounded, _) = super::bound_content(&t, MAX_DESCRIPTION_CHARS); super::redact_wrap(manager, &bounded) }) — the truncation flag is dropped; the model sees no footer noting the description was cut.
suggested_fix: Surface truncation the same way redact_and_wrap does: pass the `truncated` flag through and append a 'description truncated to N chars' suffix to the wrapped output.

issue: resolve_session_path uses .map_err(|e| format!("...: {e}")) twice instead of structured error context
evidence: let dir = crate::discovery::aleph_home_dir().map_err(|e| format!("cannot resolve aleph home: {e}"))?.join(...); tokio::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).await.map_err(|e| format!("cannot create session dir: {e}"))?;
suggested_fix: If this tool is allowed to grow to anyhow, wrap with .context("cannot resolve aleph home") and .context("cannot create session dir"). If the project standard is `thiserror` (libraries), define a `BrowserSessionError` enum and map into it. The current `String` error type loses the underlying io::Error / discovery error kind, which makes production triage harder.

issue: `auto_detect_script` interpolates `path` into the shell via `shell_single_quote`; the auto-detection script that follows is then concatenated with that escaped fragment under no further quoting. The escape is correct, but the pattern is fragile (a future refactor that changes how the path fragment is concatenated could re-introduce shell injection).
evidence: let py_target = path.map(str::trim).filter(|p| p.ends_with(".py") && !p.is_empty()).map(shell_single_quote); ... let py_fallback = match py_target { Some(q) => format!("python3 -m py_compile {q}"), ... };
suggested_fix: Either build the script as a `Vec<String>` and join with explicit shell-escaping at each call, or accept the path through an env var (already isolated by the sandbox) and reference it as `$PY_TARGET` so shell-quoting is unambiguous. Today the test pins the result string and any future refactor can silently lose the quoting.

issue: `let service = self.service.lock().await;` is acquired at the top of `call` and held for the entire await chain — every other cron-tool caller on the same `SharedCronService` blocks until the action returns.
suggested_fix: For the read actions (`list`, `get`, `runs`) take the lock per-call inside the arm and drop it before formatting the response. For `create`/`update`/`delete`/`run` the lock is necessary, but `Run` triggers another scheduler tick which may re-enter the lock downstream — verify the service's `run_job` is safe to call while the tool still holds the guard (or release the guard first).

issue: `next_id` is `wrapping_add(1).max(1)` so after 4_294_967_295 issued snapshots per process it wraps to 0, then `max(1)` lifts it to 1 — colliding with whatever snapshot id is currently active in any live lane. The `s{08x}` format is 8 hex digits so the per-process lifetime number is bounded by `2^32` snapshots (each AX snapshot has a `max_elements ≤ 500` cost) and collision is practically unreachable, but the guard is fragile: a single stray `issue` in a test that bypasses the wrapper could push the counter and never reset it.
evidence: `store.next_id = store.next_id.wrapping_add(1).max(1);`
suggested_fix: Document the 2^32 cap explicitly, or reset `next_id` to 1 when evicting a lane whose id equals `next_id - 1` to make wraparound observable.

issue: `walk_ax` allocates a fresh `serde_json::Map` via `affordance_fields(node)` for every AX-node match. `success_output_ax` then calls `affordance_fields(node)` a *second* time on the best match to splice into the output. Two Maps per hot match on a 10k-node Chromium tree is wasted allocation.
evidence: `out.push(AxMatch { ... affordances: affordance_fields(node), });` in `walk_ax`, followed by `map.extend(m.affordances.clone());` and `map.extend(best.affordances.clone());` in `success_output_ax`. The Map is then `clone()`-extended, not moved.
suggested_fix: Compute `affordance_fields` once and move it into the output by reference, or build the final JSON inline during the walk.

issue: Production `.expect("invariant: main_key has exactly one element after split")` in the `key_combo` arm. Upstream `keys.is_empty()` guard makes the invariant true today, but any future refactor that breaks it panics the worker (no structured refusal).
evidence: `let key = main_key.first().expect("invariant: main_key has exactly one element after split");`
suggested_fix: Replace with `let Some(key) = main_key.first() else { return Ok(Some(DesktopOutput { success:false, message:Some("internal: key_combo produced an empty main key".into()), .. })); };` — fail-closed structured error instead of panic.

issue: `ComputerUseLock::release()` does synchronous `std::fs::remove_file` and `read_to_string` from `Drop`, which fires when `SessionLockGuard` drops at the end of an async tool call. The lock file is small and writes are short, but it is blocking I/O on the tokio worker thread — a violation of the codebase's own `use tokio::sync::Mutex` / "never hold std Mutex across .await" rule, just for the inverse case.
evidence: `impl Drop for ComputerUseLock { fn drop(&mut self) { if self.held { if let Err(e) = self.release() { ... } } } }` calls `fs::remove_file` and `fs::read_to_string` synchronously. The `Drop` fires when the outer `SessionLockGuard` drops, which is at the end of an async `call()` body.
suggested_fix: Move release to an explicit `async fn release_async` invoked from a tokio context, with `Drop` only setting a `dirty` flag.

issue: `draw_digit` panics with `.expect("invariant: digit is derived from ASCII 0-9")` if the digit is out of range. The caller (`draw_label`) sources digits from `n.to_string().bytes().map(|b| (b - b'0') as usize)`, so a future change that lets user input flow in (e.g. an element index from a non-numeric source) would panic the worker.
evidence: `let glyph = GLYPHS.get(digit).expect("invariant: digit is derived from ASCII 0-9");`
suggested_fix: Return a `Result<(), ()>` from `draw_digit`; on out-of-range draw the badge background only and skip the glyph.

issue: `fold` reports only the *first* encountered `UnknownReason` when multiple predicates carry distinct unknown reasons (e.g. one `target_missing`, one `observation_unavailable`). The model sees one reason and may act on it while the other predicate had a different cause worth knowing.
evidence: `PredStatus::Unknown(r) => unknown = unknown.or(Some(r)),` — first-write wins; later Unknown reasons are dropped.
suggested_fix: Surface all distinct unknown reasons as an array on the overall status, or pick the most-actionable one (`target_missing` over `observation_unavailable`).

issue: `MAX_PATCH_BYTES = 4 MiB`, `MAX_PATCH_OPS = 500`, `MAX_ADD_LINES = 100_000`, `MAX_ADD_BODY_BYTES = 16 MiB` are all inline `const` inside function bodies (e.g. `plan_add` declares `MAX_ADD_LINES` and `MAX_ADD_BODY_BYTES` inside the function). Discoverability and adjustability suffer.
evidence: const MAX_ADD_LINES: usize = 100_000; const MAX_ADD_BODY_BYTES: usize = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
suggested_fix: Hoist all four to module-level `pub(crate) const` next to `MAX_PATCH_BYTES` so a single block enumerates the envelope's resource ceiling.

issue: `unique_dest` loops `for n in 1..usize::MAX` — a directory holding ~4 billion same-named entries will spin for many seconds before terminating. The file-existence probe is O(N) syscall per iteration.
evidence: for n in 1..usize::MAX { ... if !candidate.exists() { return candidate; } }
suggested_fix: Cap iterations at a smaller constant (e.g. 1_000_000) and return an error past that, or use a HashSet-based dedup so the loop is O(1) probe.

issue: `execute_organize` silently discards directory-entry errors via `filter_map(|e| e.ok())` — EACCES or removed-mid-walk entries vanish with no count, unlike `ops::execute_list` (which reports `skipped`).
evidence: let entries: Vec<_> = fs::read_dir(&canonical) ... .filter_map(|e| e.ok()) .collect();
suggested_fix: Mirror `execute_list`: count dropped entries and disclose in the message ("Skipped N unreadable entries").

issue: `read_text_file`'s 100 MB cap and `FileWriteTool::call`'s 32 MB cap and `FileReadTool::new`'s 100 MB cap are three independent inline constants. Drift between any two of them surfaces as a tool-family inconsistency the model has to discover empirically.
evidence: const MAX_EDIT_BYTES: u64 = 100 * 1024 * 1024; ... const MAX_WRITE_CONTENT_BYTES: usize = 32 * 1024 * 1024; ... max_read_size: 100 * 1024 * 1024
suggested_fix: Promote these to `pub(crate) const` in `text.rs` (next to `MAX_LINE_CHARS`) so the read/write/edit family shares one named limit and any future adjustment is single-site.

issue: `execute_copy` claims a single `lock_path_pair` on (source, destination) for the entire recursive walk — including all `fs::copy` blocking syscalls — so a concurrent edit anywhere in the source subtree waits for the full copy to finish, and a concurrent destination write waits for it too.
evidence: let _path_guards = lock_path_pair(&from_canonical, &to_canonical).await; ... copy_dir_recursive(...)
suggested_fix: Lock per-entry inside the recursive walker, not once at the top. The `batch_move` / `organize` loop already does the per-item version; copy should follow suit. Same comment applies to `execute_move`'s single-source/destination lock.

issue: `copy_dir_recursive` treats a `canonicalize` failure on a non-symlink as `tally.note_unresolvable(...)` — good — but the `Ok(())` early-return path on a SYMLINK's canonicalize failure hard-errors the whole copy. A dangling symlink in the tree aborts the entire batch.
evidence: let canonical = match fs::canonicalize(&from_path) { Ok(canonical) => canonical, Err(e) if is_symlink => { return Err(ToolError::Execution(format!("Failed to canonicalize symlink: {e}"))) } Err(e) => { tally.note_unresolvable(&from_path); continue; } };
suggested_fix: Dangling symlinks should be reported as unresolvable (or skipped), not fatal — the parallel `execute_list` and `execute_stats` paths already do so.

issue: `resolve_for_removal` calls blocking `std::fs::symlink_metadata` and `safe_normalize` (which calls blocking `canonicalize`) inside what is otherwise the async path-resolver layer. Called from async fns (`execute_move`, `execute_delete`).
evidence: let is_symlink = std::fs::symlink_metadata(&expanded) ... let canon_parent = safe_normalize(parent)
suggested_fix: Either make `resolve_for_removal` async and use `tokio::fs::symlink_metadata`, or accept it as a synchronous helper but document the cost — currently it's silently borrowed into every async move/delete call.

issue: `render_window` relies on three `.expect(...)` panics labelled 'invariant' (lines 218, 263, 288). The invariants are documented but if violated the entire async task panics on the tokio worker — a model that crafts a request forcing an off-by-one (e.g. `offset=0` combined with the `max(1)` clamp) would crash the tool, not return an error.
evidence: lines.get(start..line_end).expect("invariant: start..line_end is clamped to lines length")
suggested_fix: Replace `expect` with `match` returning a `FileReadOutput { success: false, message: "...", .. }`. Invariant violations are a defensive surface, not a reason to panic the worker.

issue: The eviction policy on `MAX_READ_CACHE_ENTRIES` overflow is `map.keys().next().cloned()` — a HashMap's iteration order is randomized, so a determined attacker model that reads10 001 distinct windows in quick succession can evict an arbitrary (not least-recently-used) entry. Documented as 'any is fine' but the cap fires every read past10 000, hammering the eviction path.
evidence: if let Some(evicted) = map.keys().next().cloned() { map.remove(&evicted); }
suggested_fix: Either accept the eviction cost and document it as a deliberate 'fingerprint, not LRU' choice, or wire in `lru::LruCache` and track recent insertions. The current comment already concedes the latter is the principled fix.

issue: `execute_search` silently drops every match whose `fs::metadata` fails (`if let Ok(metadata) = ...`). A search result with all entries unreadable returns the same shape as an empty search, with no skipped count.
evidence: if let Ok(metadata) = fs::metadata(&path) { matched += 1;
suggested_fix: Track a `skipped_unreadable: usize` and disclose it in the result message, matching `execute_list` / `execute_stats`.

issue: Arc<std::sync::RwLock<...>> held briefly inside an async fn; the lock IS dropped before .await, so it does not block across await — but std::sync RwLock contention under concurrent tool calls will block the executor thread.
evidence: let reg = self.registry.read().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()); ... provider.generate(request).await ...
suggested_fix: Switch to tokio::sync::RwLock (re-exported as AsyncRwLock) for read-heavy concurrent access; the brief-lock pattern is otherwise correct.

issue: Same std::sync::RwLock-in-async pattern as audio_generate; safe under the brief-lock discipline but inconsistent with speech_generate which already notes 'lock must be dropped before any .await'.
evidence: let registry = self.registry.read().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
suggested_fix: Use AsyncRwLock from sync_primitives for uniform async-friendly locking; add a #[allow(clippy::await_holding_lock)] only if a sync lock is justified.

issue: The `meeting` URL is forwarded to the configured bridge as a JSON-RPC arg with no SSRF/host validation at the tool layer; trust is delegated entirely to the bridge.
evidence: pub meeting: Option<String>, ... if GoogleMeetAction::Join => Self::require(&args.meeting, "meeting", "join")?; (no host check before dispatch_to_bridge)
suggested_fix: If the bridge is the only authoritative gate, document that explicitly on the field (and the DESCRIPTION). Otherwise, mirror `a2a_tools::add` and `media_send::preflight` and run `validate_url_async(&args.meeting, &SsrfPolicy::default())` before dispatch — cheap, defense-in-depth, and surfaces the failure to the model rather than the bridge.

issue: Dead-branch defensive code: `None => continue` cannot fire because Null/Array/Object are already handled above and value_to_string returns Some for every other Value variant.
evidence: _ => match value_to_string(raw) { Some(v) => v, None => continue, }
suggested_fix: Replace with an unreachable!() or document why the branch is defensive; the current shape reads as 'silent skip on unknown type'.

issue: An `expect("invariant: name came from presets iterator")` in production code; the invariant holds for the current call shape but is not enforced by types.
evidence: let p = cfg.presets.get(name).expect("invariant: name came from presets iterator");
suggested_fix: Iterate entries once and project directly (`cfg.presets.iter().filter(...).map(|(name, p)| { ... })`) — keeps the invariant in the iterator and removes the expect. The two-pass `filter+collect` followed by `get` is a duplication the type system cannot verify.

issue: SSRF pre-flight uses `SsrfPolicy::default()` rather than the operator's configured policy.
evidence: let ssrf_policy = SsrfPolicy::default();
suggested_fix: Same fix as `a2a_tools` — pull the policy from `Config::ssrf` so the operator's allowlist/audit reaches the tool face. The pre-flight is also a defense-in-depth check that `safe_fetch` re-runs; consistent policy values keep the two from drifting.

issue: `RetrievalScoringConfig` and `ExpansionConfig` are accepted by `new_with_config` and applied to `NoteFactRetrieval`, but there is no equivalent path to set `similarity_threshold` — meaning the retrieval layer's actual similarity gate cannot be tuned from the public constructor that the doc claims supports it.
evidence: pub fn new_with_config(database, embedder, similarity_threshold, rerank_config, scoring_config, expansion_config) — `similarity_threshold` is consumed only by the dead-code `_threshold = ...` line above.
suggested_fix: Wire `_threshold` into `NoteFactRetrieval::with_similarity_threshold` (or equivalent), or remove it from the constructor signature. As written, the constructor signature is a promise the implementation cannot keep.

issue: The `similarity_threshold` parameter is computed and assigned to `_threshold` but never used, leaving the threshold config knob exposed in the API surface without effect.
evidence: let _threshold = similarity_threshold.unwrap_or(Self::DEFAULT_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD);
suggested_fix: Either thread `_threshold` into the underlying `NoteIndexer`/retrieval layer, or remove the unused parameter and constant from the public constructor `new_with_config` and the struct doc. The current state suggests a half-completed change.

issue: `FactResult::path` is a plain `String` and the session-raw branch silently substitutes an empty string when `raw.path.is_none()` — a path the rest of the model surface treats as a valid (empty) file reference.
evidence: .filter(|r| r.path.is_some()) ... path: raw.path.unwrap_or_default(),
suggested_fix: Make `FactResult::path` an `Option<String>` (skip-serializing when `None`), and filter out rows whose path is `None` rather than coercing to `""`. The current `unwrap_or_default()` is exactly the leak the `filter` immediately above it was written to prevent — the filter runs after `unwrap_or_default` would have produced an empty string only when `None`, but reading the code, the two lines disagree on whether an empty path is a real fact.

issue: `similarity_score` is used as both `confidence` and `similarity_score` in the projection below, duplicating a numeric value under two field names — the model gets no signal that the two numbers are identical.
evidence: confidence: f.similarity_score.unwrap_or(0.0), similarity_score: f.similarity_score.unwrap_or(0.0),
suggested_fix: Drop one or rename one (`similarity_score → score` and `confidence → confidence` when a real confidence is available). Today they are guaranteed equal, which makes the schema effectively twice as wide as the data.

issue: MAX_NOTE_BODY_CHARS = 1 MiB caps create content, but `append` accepts an unbounded `facts: Vec<String>` — a steered model can append millions of small facts and exhaust disk without any single body exceeding the cap.
evidence: let new_facts = args.facts.clone().unwrap_or_default();
suggested_fix: Apply a per-call cap on total facts bytes (mirror MAX_NOTE_BODY_CHARS for the append payload) and an upper bound on facts.len().

issue: MAX_ORIENT_TOKENS = 64 * 1024 is a hard cap with no test that asserts the cap is actually applied — a future refactor that drops the min() call would walk the entire corpus into a single tool result.
evidence: let max_tokens = requested.min(MAX_ORIENT_TOKENS);
suggested_fix: Add a unit test that constructs a tool with default_budget.max_tokens = usize::MAX and asserts the read_snapshot call receives the clamped budget.

issue: TAIL bound of 80 bytes is a magic value with no comment — short enough that a 90-byte prefix could be split across the window boundary and the second half of the prefix still lands in the visible window before the next flush.
evidence: const TAIL: usize = 80; no justification for the size in the comment or test
suggested_fix: Either widen the search window to max(prefix lengths) + a small safety margin and document the bound, or add a unit test that pins a prefix at byte 80-1 to lock the boundary behaviour.

issue: printpdf's warnings buffer (&mut Vec::new()) is discarded — any font-substitution or layout warnings emitted during save are silently lost.
evidence: .save(&PdfSaveOptions::default(), &mut Vec::new());
suggested_fix: Pass a named Vec, log non-empty contents at debug!, and surface font-substitution warnings in the tool output for CJK-fallback visibility.

issue: Magic constant `0.4` in wrap_text (units_per_mm) controls CJK-vs-Latin width estimation; no derivation or reference, and the comment ('Approximate') leaves the calibration unknowable.
evidence: let units_per_mm = 0.4 / (font_size / 12.0);
suggested_fix: Either derive from a documented monospace font metric (e.g. reference char width at 12pt) or expose as a named const with the empirical origin documented; ideally a constant per font rather than global.

issue: mail_search limit is clamped at the I/O boundary (clamp(1, 200)) but the underlying provider call still receives a potentially-huge filtered set before clamping — the clamp is at the tool boundary, not where the native bridge enumerates.
evidence: let limit = args.limit.unwrap_or(20).clamp(1, 200); pim.mail_search(query, args.folder.as_deref(), limit)
suggested_fix: Document the contract that the provider respects the limit, or push the clamp into the bridge wrapper so a custom backend can't bypass it.

issue: MAX_RUNNING_GLOBAL=32 + MAX_RUNNING_PER_SESSION=8 caps are silently rejected with no operator-visible telemetry — a runaway consumer model hit at 32 in a 2-session install, but the only log is a `tracing::warn!` absent here, only at the consumer's caller.
evidence: RegisterOutcome::TooManyRunning returns the limit but the registry does not record the rejection; the cap is enforced but the operator never learns the fleet-wide ceiling was hit until they read the model's tool result.
suggested_fix: Optional: emit a `tracing::warn!(metric="registry.rejected", global=…, per_session=…)` so fleet-wide ceiling trips are observable in production logs.

issue: relevance_score is hard-coded to 1.0 for every fragment — the field is named 'relevance' but carries no scoring signal, so a downstream model that ranks hits by this field gets a meaningless order.
evidence: relevance_score: 1.0 (line 115); comment on the BT-D-R4-01 fix says FTS5/BM25 is tracked separately
suggested_fix: Either rename the field to a non-ranking name (`from_query: bool` or remove the `relevance_` prefix) or compute a real score (substring position, hit count) — the current name invites misuse.

issue: namespace_explicit_project_id uses a sanitized actor slug; if the actor id contains only non-ASCII the slug collapses to all-dashes and two distinct non-ASCII actors collide on the same namespaced id.
evidence: fn namespace_explicit_project_id — `slug: String = actor.chars().map(|c| if c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '-' || c == '_' { c } else { '-' }).collect();`
suggested_fix: Use a hash of the actor (or a short hash suffix) when the slug is all-dashes to preserve the cross-principal separation even for non-ASCII actor names.

issue: MAX_SESSION_SEARCH_RESULTS = 100 is the hard cap; clamp happens at line 178 and is the only defence against a model passing usize::MAX, but the constant is undocumented and there's no test pinning the behaviour.
evidence: const MAX_SESSION_SEARCH_RESULTS: usize = 100;
suggested_fix: Add a unit test that requests max_results = usize::MAX and asserts the returned hit count is bounded by 100.

issue: Per-session get_history is awaited sequentially inside a for-loop, so message_limit > 0 serializes N round-trips.
evidence: for row in &mut rows { if let Some(legacy_key) = ... { match self.context.session_store().get_history(&legacy_key, Some(message_limit)).await { ... } } }
suggested_fix: Use futures::stream / try_join_all / buffer_unordered to fetch histories concurrently; cap concurrency to a small bounded value.

issue: Fire-and-forget default timeout of 300s is a magic literal not exposed as a constant (sibling tools use named constants).
evidence: timeout_secs: if args.timeout_seconds > 0 { Some(u64::from(args.timeout_seconds)) } else { Some(300) // Default 5 min for fire-and-forget
suggested_fix: Extract to a named const (e.g. DEFAULT_FIRE_AND_FORGET_TIMEOUT_SECS) alongside MAX_CROSS_SESSION_MESSAGE_CHARS for parity.

issue: create() writes SKILL.md then calls ensure_dir_registered + reload_file, but if reload_file errors the SKILL.md is already on disk and the registry may not see it — a partial-success state the caller gets back as an AlephError without knowing whether the file exists.
evidence: tokio::fs::write(&path, &full).await...; self.system.ensure_dir_registered(root).await; self.system.reload_file(&path).await.map_err(...)?;
suggested_fix: Surface the on-disk state in the error message ('wrote SKILL.md to X, but reload failed: Y') so the caller knows the file landed; current code propagates only the reload error.

issue: Drop fence uses `let _ = store.release_lock(&task_id, &agent_id).await;` — failure swallowed silently so a stuck lock from a dropped leader run is invisible to operators (zombie reclaimer is the silent backstop).
evidence: let _ = store.release_lock(&task_id, &agent_id).await; — no logging on Err despite the rest of the function logging release failures.
suggested_fix: Mirror the warning-logging shape used a few lines above (`tracing::warn!(... "could not release leftover lock")`) so post-drop lock leaks are diagnosable.

issue: "conclude" mode accepts an empty outcome when neither conclusion nor content is provided.
evidence: let conclusion = args.conclusion.unwrap_or(args.content); — no emptiness check; an empty SessionOutcome is forwarded to coordinator.finalize.
suggested_fix: Require at least one of conclusion/content in conclude mode; refuse with a tool error otherwise.

issue: Comment claims IPv4 redaction targets 'any private range' (SSRF surface) but the implementation redacts every dotted-quad — a model reading '[REDACTED:ip]' on a legitimate public address then propagates the false positive.
evidence: Line 138: `// IPv4 (any private range)`; scan_ipv4 has no range filter.
suggested_fix: Align the doc with the implementation: reword to 'any IPv4 shape' (broader, safer direction) or narrow the regex to 10/172.16-31/192.168 (correct, narrower).

issue: scan_ipv4 matches ANY dotted-quad (e.g. 999.999.999.999), not a valid IPv4 — group_len <= 3 is checked but octet value 0-255 is not.
evidence: fn scan_ipv4 — `if group_len > 3 { return None; }` is the only bound; no 0-255 range check per octet; comment claims 'any private range' but the function matches any IPv4
suggested_fix: Either tighten the regex to enforce 0-255 per octet (would need a state machine) or change the comment to 'any IPv4 shape' and accept the false positives; the redaction is harm-permissive but the wording now lies to the reader.

issue: A fresh reqwest::Client is constructed on every probe call — no connection-pool reuse across calls.
evidence: let mut req = reqwest::Client::new().get(...).timeout(...)
suggested_fix: Hold a single reqwest::Client inside LocalVoiceTool (constructed once) and clone per call.

issue: Reachability probe timeout of 3 seconds is an undocumented magic literal.
evidence: .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(3));
suggested_fix: Lift to a named const (e.g. LOCAL_VOICE_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECS) with a docstring explaining the trade-off.

issue: Cancel / pause / resume arms all snapshot tasks first, then re-fetch each task before writing — but the in-flight count and the per-task status are computed from the same snapshot, so a task that flipped Running → Done between snapshot and re-fetch is counted as in-flight in the message while being skipped in the write loop.
evidence: Status writes iterate `tasks` snapshot and call `get_task(&task.id)` per iteration; `in_flight` is incremented from the original `live_status` before the re-fetch, but the cancel arm at line 1103 uses the same logic. Minor: the 'in-flight' branch only fires when the snapshot said InProgress AND the re-fetch confirmed it (otherwise it's been promoted to terminal and the snapshot counter is stale).
suggested_fix: Recompute `in_flight` from the re-fetched statuses, not the snapshot — already done in pause (line 1171) but cancel still relies on `live_status == InProgress` which is correct; this is observation, not a defect.

issue: `read_asset`'s fallback `tokio::fs::metadata(&canvas_dir)` to distinguish "asset missing" from "canvas missing" is unlocked and can yield a misleading exact message if a concurrent `delete` lands between the two syscalls.
evidence: match tokio::fs::metadata(&canvas_dir).await { Ok(_) => Err(... "asset ..."), Err(_) => Err(... "canvas ...") }
suggested_fix: Either collapse both messages to a single NotFound, or take the per-canvas read-side slot (currently absent) for the two syscalls.

issue: Silent recovery from a poisoned `std::sync::Mutex` via `unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())` — if a thread panicked mid-insert, the slot map can be observed in a partial state and the panic root cause is hidden.
evidence: self.slots.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
suggested_fix: Keep the recovery (the `MetaLocks` precedent is defensible for a metadata table) but at minimum `tracing::error!(...)` the poison before draining so the panic is observable in logs.

issue: Same poisoned-mutex silent-recovery pattern as `doc_io.rs`; a panic in one selection setter hides its own cause and exposes the table to potentially-stale state.
evidence: .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) (lines 99 and 109, in `set` and `get`)
suggested_fix: Log the poison before draining, or convert to `tokio::sync::Mutex` and propagate as an error variant instead of swallowing.

issue: Sweep failures inside `apply` are logged and discarded; an asset directory that becomes unwritable will accumulate orphans indefinitely with no signal beyond a `warn!` per apply.
evidence: if let Err(e) = self.sweep_assets_with(id, &referenced).await { warn!(...) }
suggested_fix: Track consecutive sweep failures per canvas and surface a doctor-style diagnostic (`core/orphan_sweep_stuck`) so an unwritable assets dir does not silently degrade.

issue: RetireOnAbandon::drop silently no-ops when no tokio runtime is current, leaving the registry entry as a zombie; the assumption that ask() is always called under a runtime is unstated and untested.
evidence: impl Drop for RetireOnAbandon { fn drop(&mut self) { drop(self.rx.take()); if !self.armed { return; } let Ok(handle) = tokio::runtime::Handle::try_current() else { return; }; ... handle.spawn(async move { manager.cancel_abandoned(&session_key).await; }); } }
suggested_fix: Either document the runtime requirement at the ask() signature (or return Err on call sites lacking a runtime), or fall back to a synchronous retire (best-effort) using sync cleanup_expired under a sync Api. Add a test that exercises the no-handle path.

issue: render() interpolates prompt/header/labels/descriptions raw into the channel text; markdown-active channels (Telegram *bold*, _italic_, ```) interpret model-supplied text — no escaping layer exists.
evidence: let mut text = format!("❓{position} {header}{}", question.prompt); ... text.push_str(&menu(&question.options)); — collapse_whitespace is applied to labels/desc but there is no markdown escape for prompt/header/menu. The header wrap is format!("[{h}] "), letting `]` in the header create overlapping brackets and any * _ ` characters in prompt reach the channel verbatim.
suggested_fix: Add a markdown-neutralising pass for the prompt/header (replace * _ ` with fullwidth equivalents, or wrap pre-formatted blocks). Threats are limited because the model is also the prompt source, but a malformed prompt from a future ask_user producer would render unexpectedly.

issue: render() applies collapse_whitespace to label/description but NOT to question.prompt or header — a prompt with embedded \n shifts the ❓ prefix formatting and breaks the user's mental model of question order on Telegram-style channels.
evidence: let mut text = format!("❓{position} {header}{}", question.prompt); — compare with menu() which calls collapse_whitespace(opt.label) and option.description.
suggested_fix: Pass question.prompt through collapse_whitespace() before formatting, or assert/document that prompts are single-line by contract (and reject multi-line at ClarificationRequest::new()).
